extracted.intended_audience: GSA offerors and contractors, federal contractors responding to MAS/FSS solicitations, members of the public and local governments affected by FEMA flood map revisions, and commenters/respondents to OMB information collections
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for submitting public comments and responding to federal information-collection notices (Paperwork Reduction Act), requirements for GSA MAS/FSS solicitation information and GSAR clauses, and notices on FEMA flood hazard determinations including appeals and inspection locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comments invited on information collections (PRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments are particularly invited on: Whether this collection of information is necessary and whether it will have practical utility; whether our estimate of the public burden of this collection of information is accurate and based on valid assumptions and methodology; ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments by the date listed; include the OMB Control number in correspondence. Comments will generally be posted without change to regulations.gov. If you cannot use regulations.gov, call or email the points of contact listed for alternate instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for submitting comments via regulations.gov / eRulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments identified by the specific information collection (e.g., “Information Collection 3090-0303, Federal Supply Schedule Solicitation Information”) to http://www.regulations.gov using the portal’s Submit a Comment link corresponding to that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 'Submit a Comment' screen instructions; include your name, company name (if any), and the information collection title/OMB control number on any attached document. To confirm receipt, check regulations.gov ~2–3 days after submission to verify posting. If you cannot submit via the portal, contact the listed FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for alternate instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice that comments will be posted without change
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments received generally will be posted without change to http://www.regulations.gov, including any personal and/or business confidential information provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include information you do not want publicly posted; commenters should be aware that submissions may become public as submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining copies of information collection documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters may obtain a copy of the information collection documents from the GSA Regulatory Secretariat Division or the General Services Administration, Regulatory Secretariat Division (MVCB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting, cite the relevant OMB Control No. (e.g., 3090-0283, 3090-0303, 3090-0308). Forms (e.g., GSA Form 850) can be downloaded from the GSA Forms Library at https://www.gsa.gov/forms by typing the form number in the search field. Contact phone/email information is provided in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection burden reporting format
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reporting burdens are reported as: Respondents; Responses per Respondent; Total Annual Responses; Hours per Response; Total Burden Hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided in notices include numerical estimates for specific collections (e.g., Respondents: 1,590; Responses per respondent: 1; Preparation hours per response: 0.50; Total response burden hours: 795). Use these line items to evaluate PRA burden estimates and to comment on their accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collected information by contracting officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The information collection consists of information used by contracting officers awarding GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) / Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) contracts in the review and evaluation of offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may address whether the information requested is necessary for evaluation and whether it has practical utility in the award process.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-84 — Discounts for Prompt Payment
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause requests an offeror to identify in their offer any discounts for early payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should state any early-payment discounts in offers; PRA burden estimates apply (example: Respondents 1,590; 0.5 hours per response).

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-87 — Delivery Prices (Alaska/Hawaii/Puerto Rico)
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause requests an offeror to identify whether or not prices submitted cover delivery f.o.b. destination in Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must indicate coverage for those jurisdictions; example PRA burden: 0.5 hours per response.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-95 — Separate Charge for Performance Oriented Packaging (POP)
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause requests an offeror, if applicable, to identify any hazardous material item (i.e., SIN or Descriptive Name of Article) being offered and the separate charge that applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when offering hazardous material items; example PRA burden: 0.5 hours per response. Note: clause applies to specific MAS solicitation large categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-96 — Separate Charge for Delivery within Consignee’s Premises
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause requests an offeror, as applicable, to identify any separate charge(s) for shipping when the delivery is within the consignee’s premises (inclusive of items that are comparable in size and weight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should list separate shipping charges where applicable; example PRA burden: 0.5 hours per response.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-97 — Parts and Service
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause requests an offeror, if applicable, to include in their offer the names and addresses of all supply and service points maintained in the geographic area in which the offeror would perform under the GSA FSS contract, and to indicate whether a complete stock of repair parts is carried at that point and whether mechanical service is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supply/service point details and availability of parts/service; example PRA burden: 0.5 hours per response.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-99 — Delivery Prices Overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause requests an offeror to identify the intended geographic area(s)/countries/zones which are covered by their offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must identify geographic coverage for overseas delivery pricing; example PRA burden: 0.5 hours per response.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-111 — EPA Registration Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause requests offerors, if applicable, to identify the manufacturer’s and/or distributor’s name and EPA Registration Number for each item offered that requires registration with the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide manufacturer/distributor names and EPA Registration Numbers where applicable; example PRA burden: 1.0 hour per response. Clause applies to specific MAS solicitation large categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR provision 552.238-118 — Single-use Plastic (SUP) Free Packaging Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision applies when the resulting contract includes supplies or products and provides the option for offerors to submit information about SUP free brand packaging and SUP free shipping packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional submission; example PRA burden: 2.1 hours per response. Offerors may provide identification information about SUP-free packaging choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR clause 552.238-119 — Single-use Plastic (SUP) Free Packaging Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause provides the option for contractors to submit information about SUP free brand packaging and SUP free shipping packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional availability reporting; example PRA burden: 20.1 hours per response (as estimated).

rubrics_metrics.name: GSAR 552.236-72 Submittals (Construction-Manager-as-Constructor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reporting burden for GSAR 552.236-72, Submittals, is estimated to average 0.50 hours per response, including time reviewing instructions, searching data sources, gathering and maintaining data, and completing/reviewing the collection of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates provided: Respondents 995; Responses per respondent 5; Total annual responses 4,975; Total response burden hours 2,488. Commenters may dispute these estimates or suggest burden-reduction measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEMA flood hazard determinations — basis and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice lists communities where addition/modification of BFEs, base flood depths, SFHA boundaries or zone designations, or regulatory floodway is appropriate because of new scientific or technical data; FIRMs and, where applicable, FIS reports have been revised and Letters of Map Revision (LOMR) issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised flood hazard information for each community is available for inspection at the online location and the respective community map repository address listed in the table; current effective FIRM and FIS reports are accessible via the FEMA Map Service Center for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEMA appeal/reconsideration procedure and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: From the date of the second publication of notification of these changes in a newspaper of local circulation, any person has 90 days to request through the community that the Deputy Associate Administrator for Insurance and Mitigation reconsider the changes. The flood hazard determination information may be changed during the 90-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for reconsideration must be submitted to the Chief Executive Officer of the community as listed in the table below. Submit comments and/or appeals to the Chief Executive Officer of the community as listed in the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEMA legal/regulatory authority and minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications are made pursuant to section 201 of the Flood Disaster Protection Act of 1973 (42 U.S.C. 4105), in accordance with the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.), and with 44 CFR part 65. The flood hazard determinations, together with the floodplain management criteria required by 44 CFR 60.3, are the minimum required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These determinations should not be construed to require communities to change any existing ordinances that are more stringent; communities may enact stricter requirements at any time or pursuant to other authorities. The FIRM and FIS report are the basis of floodplain management measures that the community is required to adopt or show evidence of having in effect to qualify for the NFIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH/committee meeting public comment submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may file written comments with the committee by forwarding the statement to the Contact Person listed on the notice. The statement should include the name, address, telephone number and when applicable, the business or professional affiliation of the interested person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details (name, phone, email, postal address) and where meeting agendas/additional info will be posted (e.g., institute home page) are provided in the notice; notify contact person in advance for reasonable accommodations to view virtual meetings.
